'V' in rows is the float of the 50-digit 'V_exact'. Normalised values at nominal ratio r are log-f-interpolated along the full curve in k (k^2+1, k^3+2: step in f(y) is not small for small y, so the actual ratio fy/x differs from nominal); 'ratio_actual' and 'V_over_x12_fy32_actual' give the raw ratio at the grid y. For 2k+1 nominal and actual ratios agree to <3e-5. k^2+1: cutoff r>=0.01, constant 0.13458 +- 0.00752; rel. change of N between x=31622777 and x=100000000 by ratio: 0.01:-0.10%, 0.02:-0.04%, 0.05:+0.00%, 0.1:-0.02%, 0.2:-0.03%, 0.4:-0.02%, 0.7:-0.01%, 1.0:-0.01%. k^3+2: cutoff r>=0.02, constant 0.13970 +- 0.00423; rel. change of N between x=31622777 and x=100000000 by ratio: 0.01:-1.63%, 0.02:-0.57%, 0.05:-0.34%, 0.1:-0.24%, 0.2:-0.34%, 0.4:-0.42%, 0.7:-0.43%, 1.0:-0.17%. 2k+1: cutoff r>=0.01, constant 0.14086 +- 0.00845; rel. change of N between x=31622777 and x=100000000 by ratio: 0.01:+0.01%, 0.02:+0.00%, 0.05:+0.00%, 0.1:+0.00%, 0.2:+0.00%, 0.4:+0.00%, 0.7:+0.00%, 1.0:+0.00%. N(r)=V/(x^(1/2) f(y)^(3/2)) is NOT constant in r: it rises with r from ~0.14 (r=0.01) to 0.167-0.184 (r=1). Stability in x at fixed r (grid rows, two largest x): 2k+1 changes by <=0.01% at every ratio (x-independent to 4 digits for x>=3e6); k^2+1 by <=0.1%; k^3+2 by -0.2%..-0.4% at r>=0.05 (-0.57% at r=0.02, -1.6% at r=0.01) per factor 3.16 in x, i.e. the k^3+2 values still drift downward with x (so its constant is probably slightly overestimated; only ~100-465 moduli). Small ratios are NOT the most informative: lower-order terms depend on the absolute size of f(y) as well. E.g. for 2k+1 N = 0.0993 (f=1e2), 0.137 (f=1e3), 0.1426 (f=1e4) at x=1e7, and 0.1357 (f=1e3), 0.1422 (f=1e4), 0.1430 (f=1e5) at x=1e8, so N depends on f at small f, not on r. For 2k+1, N(r) also has non-smooth wiggles of size ~0.002-0.003 (dense checkpoints in raw/2k+1_*.json: a dip near r~0.25-0.35, a maximum 0.1871 near r~0.85) that no low-order polynomial in r or sqrt(r) captures. EXTRAPOLATION IS MODEL DEPENDENT: polynomial-in-r models give 0.1408-0.1454 (k^2+1), 0.142-0.146 (k^3+2), 0.147-0.149 (2k+1) while models containing sqrt(r) (preferred by leave-one-out cross-validation for all three f) give 0.135-0.139, 0.139-0.140, 0.141-0.144. The reported 'uncertainty' includes this model spread, hence it is large (0.004-0.008); the OLS intercept errors alone are only ~0.001-0.002. A sqrt(r) leading correction (relative size ~ (Y/x)^(1/2)) is suggested by the data but not proven. SUPPLEMENTARY direct readings at the largest x=1e8, outside the stability-tested fit (use as a cross-check only): k^2+1: N is ~0.1395 (range 0.1390-0.1403, 217 values of k) for 1e4<=f(y)<1e5, i.e. r<=1e-3, and 0.1405 for 1e5<=f<1e6, i.e. N flattens at ~0.1395 as r->0 (and is lower, 0.129 mean, for f<1e3 where the f-dependent corrections dominate); 2k+1: N ~ 0.1422-0.1430 for 1e-4<=r<=1e-3; k^3+2: N ~ 0.141 mean (0.1394-0.1438) for 1e5<=f<1e6, still drifting down with x. Exponent fits: at fixed x, d ln V/d ln f(y) is 1.53-1.55 over the whole grid (not 1.5) because N(r) rises with r; the fixed-ratio exponent alpha+beta is 2.000 (2k+1), 1.9993 (k^2+1), 1.994 (k^3+2); its quoted OLS se does not include the systematic x-drift (k^3+2 drift is the reason for 1.994). The single-modulus sum_l E^2 includes q > x moduli only in the interpolation tail (k with f(k)>x) used for log-f interpolation of N; rows with f(y)<=x never use them except at ratio 1.0 where the nominal value is interpolated.
